findings.topic: Instance identity and independent execution recovery
findings.assessment: Add a deep instance lifecycle module with a closed start/inspect/stop interface; hide safe-handle directory admission, lifetime lock, image/config receipts, host launch journal and adopt-or-quarantine inside its implementation. Add immutable instance/storage identity and a root incarnation without collapsing RuntimeIncarnation, RoleEpoch, ScopeEpoch, WorkspaceGeneration, persistent store or execution identity. The host journal observes owned resources and does not write controller task state. Qualify host-supervisor death before/after acknowledgement separately from controller and root-init death.

findings.topic: Paths, sockets, environment and runtime binding
findings.assessment: Construct namespace-local configuration from an admitted host-to-root projection; current canonical absolute paths, Unix path-length bound, expected transport paths, auth environment references and persisted policy identities cannot simply be copied to /state or /run. Keep role sockets/credentials selectively projected and pin image/tool/helper/mount/environment identities. Current profiles clear environment and isolate HOME/CODEX_HOME; a root plan must additionally own role XDG/tmp/cache/build/Git/Kata locations and credential renewal. Qualify restore/rebind across root incarnation and reject aliases/traversal.

findings.topic: Separate/shared servers, all tools and networking
findings.assessment: Use current separate topology and own-executor check as the first root adapter. Its remote environment registration is a useful seam, not proof that every shell/filesystem/MCP/patch/helper/background path stays in the intended tool capsule. Independently qualify those paths, descriptor inheritance, denied parent/peer/root-loopback access, scoped participant identity and provider egress/renewal. Existing provider Unix-to-private-loopback forwarding needs an instance-scoped external connector; private namespaces alone supply no routing. Keep new shared-server qualification separate.

findings.topic: Host cgroup admission, survivors and storage headroom
findings.assessment: Current launch commands/records do not express host-owned instance/trusted/Attempt cgroup allocation, pre-fork placement or filesystem/inode quotas. Add them behind the closed host lifecycle/execution interface; retain independently owned cgroup and storage receipts. Qualify cancellation to observed subtree emptiness, survivor accounting after lock release, and A exhausting its allocation while B commits/checkpoints SQLite and retains artifacts. Current cgroup namespace option in generic capsule.py is not resource limits; its destination-prefix check is unsuitable for agent-controlled plans. Do not expose arbitrary bind or bwrap arguments.

findings.topic: Private tmux and trusted operator ingress
findings.assessment: Add an instance-private tmux socket and incarnation-bound PTY/relay adapter. Leave TMUX/TMUX_PANE, tmux sockets, controlling-terminal descriptors and general app-server access outside participant tools. Existing UI gateway is root-local loopback plus a controller-bound principal; qualify controlled host forwarding, exact saved-thread attachment, literal bracketed-paste delivery/admission correlation, detach/reattach and isolation. Views remain disposable observers of controller-owned executions.

Project the complete controller persistent directory: SQLite/WAL/SHM, ownership/configuration and visible-input retention, plus separately retained Git/artifacts/runtime/monitor records. Keep WAL/FULL, controller single-writer ownership and database exclusion from workers. Qualify supported online/quiesced backup and explicit older-backup authority rotation/external-effect reconciliation; file copying or killing root is not a checkpoint. Add the Codex-first monitor adapter using pinned binding and separate ingestion/review/delivery cursors; migrate host monitor only at an explicitly admitted custody handoff with retained receipts/gaps. TraeCLI remains future.

Retain the common controller-owned workspace interface with private complete Git metadata and exact Candidate identity. The current gate serializes physical landing within one controller and CAS-updates its local canonical ref. It is not cross-instance remote landing arbitration. Use separate destinations initially; any common remote target needs an independently qualified shared landing authority or conditional update/reconciliation adapter. jj remains optional ticket07 qualification; mutable change IDs cannot replace verification identity.
